toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The August drop is almost entirely a cooling failure on floors 6-8. Chiller CH-2 failed on 4 August and wasn't fixed until 19 August. Rooms ran at 26-29°C, against a set point of 22. Floors 6-8 scores fell from 8.6 to 7.4, and room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Scores for stays ending 5-20 August were 6.8, then recovered to 8.4 once cooling returned. Floors 1-5 were essentially flat at 8.5. Of 74 negative comments, 56 were about heat, all from floors 6-8. Front-desk temperature complaints went from 1 to 24.

Cleanliness scores are flat at 8.6-8.7, and in-house inspection pass rates are unchanged at 95-96%. Kiosk use, queue times and check-in scores are also steady. So don't give notice to Orrin and don't pull the kiosks. The evidence doesn't support either move. Don't exclude the August floors 6-8 responses from the reported score either. That would hide a real failure.

Next steps: restore the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spares on site, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. The 6% rate rise is unproven as a cause. Its effect can't be separated from the usual August dip in value scores, so keep watching value scores. I'm fairly confident in this, and I didn't collect any extra evidence.
